# C10 — Underused Language Primitives

*Level 1 card. 6 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from not using available optimized language features, standard library functions, or runtime-specific constructs that would accomplish the same task more efficiently. This includes manually reimplementing functionality available as C-optimized built-ins (skipping built-ins), choosing a less efficient built-in when a faster one exists (inefficient choice), using per-element loops when bulk/vectorized primitives exist (missing bulk usage), building strings via repeated concatenation instead of join (inefficient string building), placing variables in scopes with unnecessary lookup overhead (inefficient scope), and using operators on custom types that trigger expensive dunder methods (hidden operator overloads).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | a hand-written loop doing bulk work a C-level primitive already does | replace the hand-written loop with the primitive that already does it |
| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | one primitive used where a cheaper primitive computes the same answer | use the cheaper construct that computes the same answer |
| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | a per-element call inside a loop that a single batched call would replace | replace the per-element operation with the batched primitive |
| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | a string grown with `+=` in a loop, where the target is aliased or the parts are many | collect the parts in a local list and join once, so the value that grows is never the aliased one |
| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | a global or builtin re-resolved through the module namespace on every iteration | alias the global or builtin to a local before the loop |
| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | an operator on a user-defined type dispatching and allocating once per element | do the arithmetic on primitives inside the loop and wrap once at the end |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C10.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C10.S6.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
